sources.role: graph generator, harness, and host Gauss-Seidel reference wrapped around the GAPBS kernel
build options (-ffp-contract=off) and the smoke and validation inputs

data_generation.graph: No inputs are read. For N nodes (N a power of two, N >= 4), node n has out-degree 1 + (n mod 3), and its out-neighbour i (i = 0 .. degree-1) is (7n + 13i + 1) mod N. The edge count is N + sum over n of (n mod 3), which is 2,097,151 for N = 2^20. Self-loops and repeated targets across different sources are kept.
data_generation.incoming_lists: The pull direction uses incoming lists built from the out-edges with a stable counting sort by target: sources are visited in ascending order and each source's edges in order of i, so every node's incoming list is in ascending source order. Sums follow that order.
data_generation.semantics: Ordered Gauss-Seidel pull PageRank in float. Start: score 1/N and contribution c_n = (1/N) / outdeg(n) for every node. Each of the iterations visits u = 0 .. N-1 in order: total = 0; for each incoming source v in list order, total += c_v; s_u = base + 0.85 * total; then c_u = s_u / outdeg(u) at once, so later nodes in the same sweep read the new c_u while sources v >= u contribute the value from the previous sweep. Epsilon is 0, so every iteration runs. The output is the score vector after the last iteration.
data_generation.validity: N must be a power of two and at least 3 (upstream static assertion; here 4 <= N <= 2^26), iterations from 1 to 1000; anything else exits 2.
data_generation.gpu_schedule: Host preprocessing (untimed) assigns each node a dependency level: 0 when it has no incoming source v < u, else 1 + the largest level among those sources. Each level is one kernel launch per sweep. Two contribution buffers hold the previous and current sweep; reads of v < u use the current buffer, reads of v >= u the previous buffer. Each node's sum runs sequentially in list order in one thread, so the result equals the sequential loop bitwise.

outputs.name: scores
outputs.layout: little-endian IEEE-754 binary32, indexed by node id 0 .. N-1, as downloaded to pinned host memory; the digest is FNV-1a 64 over these bytes

scores.comparison: |actual - expected| <= 1e-5 * expected, evaluated in float, for every node; non-finite actual or expected values fail
scores.source: the per-node relative bound in private Loom's gapbs-pagerank-smoke.h (every score exceeds the positive base score, so one relative bound covers every node)
scores.oracle: oracle.cpp: an independent sequential host implementation of the ordered Gauss-Seidel loop that regenerates the graph itself
scores.observed: the GPU scores are expected to match the oracle bitwise (same float operations in the same order, --fmad=false, -ffp-contract=off); the check still applies the upstream tolerance

tolerances.cross_invocation: two Direct and two Graph invocations must produce bitwise-identical scores

timing_scope.application: upload of the incoming CSR (offsets and sources), out-degrees, and level schedule from pinned host memory; score and contribution initialization; all 20 Gauss-Seidel sweeps; download of the scores to pinned host memory
timing_scope.compute: score and contribution initialization and all 20 sweeps with graph and schedule resident; no transfers
timing_scope.excluded: graph generation, incoming-CSR construction, level computation, copies into pinned buffers, allocation, CUDA Graph construction, warmups, the CPU oracle, and output checking
